calls.head: Nowhere to hide for Rantanen
calls.body: At home, the Blackhawks keep sending Frondell’s line (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jeff Blashill has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Stars’ first line is Robertson, Hintz and Rantanen.
calls.call: The Blackhawks’ L2 (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen) spends at least 48% of its 5-on-5 time against the Stars’ first line, against about 33% with no line matching.
calls.nums: At home: 63% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 33% with no line matching

chips.tip: Chicago’s L2 (Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen) at home: 63% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Chicago home games this season, 4 games, 47 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 33% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

calls.happened: Chicago’s L2 (Bertuzzi, Frondell, Teräväinen) spent 49% of its 5-on-5 time against Dallas’s L1 (3:37 of 7:23). The call needed 48%, halfway from the 33% it would get with no line matching to its home habit of 63%.

lane.tip: Share of this group’s 5-on-5 time against that line tonight (the filled dot). The ring is the call: halfway from what it would get with no line matching (the tick) to its home habit (the dotted mark), since part of any habit is luck. Reaching the ring holds the call; past the tick is partly; otherwise it didn’t happen.

calls.title: Blashill got his matchup
calls.plain: Chicago sent Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen out against the Stars’ first line for 49% of their 5-on-5 time, far more than the 33% they’d get with no line matching.
calls.said: Jeff Blashill would send Bertuzzi, Frondell and Teräväinen out against the Stars’ first line again

calls.head: Who drives the play: the Stars
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Stars have been around the middle of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. The ice should tilt the Stars’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.
calls.call: The Stars get the bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances.

calls.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
calls.body: On the power play, Dallas is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Every penalty the Blackhawks take could cost them.

surprises.head: A shutout for Jake Oettinger
surprises.body: Oettinger stopped all 19 shots, worth 2.8 expected goals. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 50 starts.

surprises.head: Chicago found the good looks for once
surprises.body: Chicago usually gets worse looks than most teams. Not tonight: an 8.8% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.1% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: Oettinger slams the door on the Blackhawks
paras: The first goal of the game would have been Dallas’, but it was taken off for offside midway through the first. They got it back early in the second, when Jason Robertson officially opened the scoring on the power play. Arttu Hyry made it 2-0 midway through the period, and he scored his second of the night early in the third to make it 3-0. Roope Hintz made it 4-0 midway through the period.
The Stars had the better of the chances, outshooting the Blackhawks 32-19. Jake Oettinger was perfect for the Stars, 19 saves on 19 shots, and Spencer Knight stopped 28 of 32 at the other end.
The Stars killed all four Blackhawks power plays. The Stars improved to 4-3-1 and climbed to fifth in the Central, while the Blackhawks dropped to 3-6-0, still last in the Central.

items.text: Connor Bedard’s seven-game point streak against Dallas ended.
Two of the preview’s three calls held.
